name: Paula Fredrikson
description: Paula Fredrikson is a historian of medicine and cognitive neuroscientist whose interdisciplinary work traces how cultural frameworks of religious experience, demonic possession, and moral panic have shaped psychiatric categorization from antiquity through the DSM era. Her book Augustine and the Jews won the AAR Award for Excellence in the Study of Religion and reshaped scholarly understanding of patristic thought's influence on Western medicine's treatment of non-normative minds. At BU she leads a dual laboratory combining archival historical analysis with fMRI imaging of how religious belief modulates threat-response circuits in the amygdala and prefrontal cortex. Her NIMH-funded comparative imaging work across denominations provided the first quantitative neuroimaging data distinguishing ecstatic religious states from prodromal psychosis symptom profiles. Fredrikson was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2016.
